roles.title: C++ Software Engineer
roles.eligibility: No graduation-year or student gate stated. No minimum years of experience stated. Posting states financial market knowledge is not required.
roles.requirements: Low-level systems programming and optimisation for extremely low-latency, high-throughput network applications | Analyse and improve performance using hardware counters and profiling tools | Deep understanding of modern computer architecture incl. cache hierarchies | Fast-packet processing in user space and kernel-bypass (Solarflare OpenOnload, TCPDirect, ef_vi, InfiniBand verbs, DPDK) | Optimising managed runtimes such as C# desirable

Posting advertises full relocation and immigration support for international candidates; candidate's UK HPI visa route costs the employer nothing.

roles.title: Quantitative Developer

roles.requirements: Deliver high-quality, well-engineered software with strong architectural awareness | End-to-end ownership from concept to delivery | Solid knowledge of algorithms, data structures and software fundamentals | Interest in quantitative finance and engineering's role within it | Identify and implement scalable improvements | Clear communication across audiences
roles.notes: Workday req R2487. Posting is written in competency language and does not name a language stack; G-Research's quant dev stack is predominantly C# and Python, so confirm C++ content at screen. Marketing page: https://www.gresearch.com/vacancies/quantitative-developer/

roles.title: Software Engineer – Trade Technology
roles.eligibility: No degree, graduation-year or minimum-years gate stated.
roles.requirements: Strong software engineering background, ideally in distributed real-time systems | Experience in at least one typed language: Java, Kotlin, C#, C++ or Rust | Production containerisation and orchestration (Kubernetes) | Robust, maintainable software with strong monitoring
roles.notes: Workday req R3160; internal req title 'Production Software Engineer'. Trading systems work; C++ is one of several accepted typed languages, not mandatory. Marketing page: https://www.gresearch.com/vacancies/production-software-engineer/

roles.title: Functional Programmer
roles.eligibility: No graduation-year or student gate stated.
roles.requirements: Experience with a functional language such as F#, Haskell, OCaml, Erlang or Elixir | Production experience with F#, C# or Python | Strong software engineering background | Familiarity with Kubernetes and relational databases | Problem-solving on complex long-term projects

roles.title: Machine Learning Engineer

roles.title: Machine Learning Engineer

roles.title: Performance Engineering Manager

roles.title: Research Engineer

roles.title: Quantitative Researcher – Experienced

roles.title: Quantitative Researcher – Postgraduate

existing_rows_audit.detail: No graduate-titled ML role exists on the board. Of the 66 live G-Research reqs (all London) there are two experienced 'Machine Learning Engineer' reqs — R2550 (https://gresearch.wd103.myworkdayjobs.com/G-Research/job/London-UK/Machine-Learning-Engineer_R2550) and R3428 — neither of which is student- or graduation-year-gated; the ML Performance track is real and open, but the '(Graduate)' qualifier and the associated '£150–250k' figure are not supported by any G-Research source. The graduates page (https://www.gresearch.com/students-graduates/graduates/) only says 'We typically launch our graduate positions in August' with no titles, dates or eligibility criteria, and no graduate scheme reqs were live on 2026-08-04 — only four internships. The comp figure should be blanked or re-sourced; no G-Research posting states any salary.

All 66 openings returned by G-Research's own Workday board (https://gresearch.wd103.myworkdayjobs.com/G-Research) on 2026-08-04 have locationsText 'London, UK' — the location facet contains London only, and there is no Dallas req of any kind, let alone an 'ML / HPC Engineer'. That exact title does not appear anywhere on the site. G-Research does have a US/Dallas presence per secondary sources, so this is not a fabricated office, but the row's role, its '$300–450k' comp figure and its source URL (the London vacancies page) are all unsupported. Dallas is also out of scope for this pass.

notes: Coverage: enumerated the full G-Research Workday board via its public JSON endpoint (66 reqs, 2026-08-04) and cross-read the marketing vacancy pages on gresearch.com/vacancies/ for every in-scope req. Every live opening is London, UK — the location facet on both the careers site and Workday contains London and nothing else. G-Research therefore has zero openings in Dublin, Amsterdam, Paris, Milan, Frankfurt, Warsaw, Zurich, Singapore, Hong Kong, Shanghai or Tokyo; www.gresearch.com/contact/ describes the firm as operating 'from our office in Central London' and lists no other address. The former /about-us/our-offices/ path 404s. A Dallas/US presence is referenced in secondary sources only and had no live reqs. No Trader-track role of any kind is open (no trader, junior trader, algo trader or execution trader titles on the board); the closest adjacency is the pair of execution/microstructure Quantitative Analyst reqs, listed under Research. Compensation: no G-Research posting states a salary or range — every one says only 'highly competitive compensation plus annual discretionary bonus' — so all comp_local fields are empty by design; do not carry over the figures currently in the sheet. Excluded as out of scope: four <6-month student internships (Quant Research, Data Science, ML Research, NLP), 16 cyber security reqs, business management, data analyst, and pure Kubernetes/network/observability infrastructure reqs. https://www.gresearch.com/vacancies/machine-learning-performance-engineer/ still resolves but the page itself states the vacancy has been filled — do not treat that URL as live. Visa: postings repeatedly state full relocation and immigration costs are covered for international candidates, and the UK HPI route is self-sponsored, so there is no work-authorisation obstacle for London.
